## Approach Deliverable

### Overview

For Assignment 7, I will start by manually creating two files, one HTML file and one JSON file, containing information about three books, including their titles, authors, publication years, and two more columns of my choosing; publisher and subject. Then, I will research and use the appropriate R packages to read both files into separate data frames. Finally, I will compare the two data frames to determine whether they contain the same data and structure.

The books I am choosing for "My Book Shelf" are *R for Data Science* by Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Garrett Grolemund, *The Catcher in the Rye* by J. D. Salinger, and *Tides: The Science and Spirit of the Ocean* by Jonathan White

## Code Base Deliverable

### Load libraries

To be able to read the HTML file, I loaded the rvest package. For the JSON data I loaded the jsonlite package. As usual, I also loaded tidyverse for other commonly used functions.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(jsonlite)
```

### Data and transformations

Load HTML file from github and create object from table

```{r}
# Read the HTML file
html_raw <- read_html("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceciliadelafuentech/DATA607-Week7/refs/heads/main/books.html")

# Extract the table
html_data <- html_raw |>
  html_element("table") |>
  html_table()

# View the data
html_data
```

Load JSON file from github and create object from the data

```{r}
# Read the JSON file
json_data <- fromJSON("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ceciliadelafuentech/DATA607-Week7/refs/heads/main/books.json")

# View the data
json_data
```

Compare the objects to check whether they are identical

```{r}
identical(html_data, json_data)

```

The output showed false so compare the dimensions and column names for each

```{r}
# Compare dimensions
dim(html_data)
dim(json_data)

# Compare column names
names(html_data)
names(json_data)
```

The dimensions are the same but the column names are different so standardize them

```{r}
# Rename HTML column names
html_clean <- html_data |>
  rename(
    title = Title,
    authors = `Author(s)`,
    year = Year,
    publisher = Publisher,
    subject = Subject
  )
```

Check if identical again and check for each column's class

```{r}
identical(html_clean, json_data)

# Compare column value class
sapply(html_clean, class)
sapply(json_data, class)
```

The comparison is still false. The values in the authors column in the JSON dataframe are lists so apply formula to return character vector

```{r}
# Transform authors values 
json_clean <- json_data |>   
  mutate(     
    authors = map_chr(authors, paste, collapse = ", ")   
  )

sapply(json_clean, class)
```

Comparison still returns false so check each object's class

```{r}
identical(html_clean, json_clean)

# Compare individual objects
class(html_clean)
class(json_clean)
```

Transform both objects to dataframes, which should make the comparison TRUE

```{r}
# Change HTML to df
html_clean <- as.data.frame(html_clean)

class(html_clean)

identical(html_clean, json_clean)
```

### Conclusion

After manually creating the HTML and JSON files about three books, I used the rvest and jsonlite packages to import the information into R. Both files produced objects with three rows and five columns, but the initial identical() comparison returned FALSE.

After checking the column names, I standardized them so both tables used the same names. However, the comparison still returned FALSE because the authors column had different data types: the HTML stored authors as character strings, while the JSON stored them as lists. I used map_chr() and paste() to combine the authors in the JSON lists into a character string to match the HTML format.

The comparison still returned FALSE because the HTML data was a tibble, while the JSON one was a data frame. I converted the HTML to a regular data frame using as.data.frame(). After these transformations, identical() returned TRUE.

This process showed that even when two files contain the same information, importing them into R can produce different structures, which does not make them identical unless transformations are made.
